meta.title: Mayya · Health Atlas
meta.subject: Mayya Grinberg
meta.scope: A public, dated compilation of the medical information available for this record. It is not a complete hospital EHR and has not been reviewed by a clinician.
meta.summary: A clear view of the diagnosis, treatments, results and lived symptoms, with the evidence behind each entry.
meta.latestStatus: The latest CT reports available in this compilation describe progression in September 2026. Pelvis/lumbar MRI screenshots available by September 23–24 describe sacral metastatic lesions. October 30 family update confirms ongoing lorlatinib, pemetrexed and bevacizumab. Response after the reviewed scans is not established.
meta.privacy: Public by link. Administrative identifiers, exact birth date, addresses, insurance details and raw scans are omitted.
limitations: Available-source compilation, not an exhaustive medical record.
Older history from conversation summaries is clearly marked family-reported.
Report findings are source-attributed; signature verification does not verify medical correctness.
This is a fixed snapshot, not live clinical monitoring.
meta.revisionNote: Added carboplatin as a separate historical treatment; previously mentioned only within the combination-regimen summary.

overview.label: Driver
overview.detail: Confirmed in July breast tissue; reported Aug 10, 2026.

overview.label: Current regimen
overview.detail: Family update Oct 30, 2026. Lorlatinib 50 mg; pemetrexed every 3 weeks.

overview.label: Last compiled

conditions.name: Metastatic ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma
conditions.description: Stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer. Never-smoking history and initial ECOG 0 were family-reported. The initial performance score is historical.

conditions.name: Recurrent left pleural effusion
conditions.status: Previously drained; loculated fluid persisted on September CT
conditions.description: Earlier malignant pleural fluid, later negative sampling, thoracenteses and PleurX are part of the reported history.

conditions.name: Sacral osseous metastatic disease
conditions.status: MRI report finding; response after MRI not available
conditions.description: S2 lesion with soft tissue/foraminal involvement and right S2 nerve-root contact or mass effect; an additional S4 lesion. Possible thecal-sac extension remains a radiology possibility. Clinical MRI dates are cropped out.

conditions.name: Low hemoglobin on latest CBC
conditions.description: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, below the laboratory reference interval 11.7–15.5. Cause is not assigned by this record.

timeline.title: Current medications updated
timeline.summary: Lorlatinib 50 mg; pemetrexed every three weeks; bevacizumab continuing. Duloxetine replaced escitalopram for nerve pain. Buprenorphine is now sublingual; occasional oxycodone. Two previous carboplatin rounds reported.

timeline.title: Food aversion and nausea
timeline.summary: Food aversion/nausea triggered by thoughts, smells or offers of food, sometimes while hungry. Onset followed either starting duloxetine or switching to sublingual buprenorphine; the user was unsure which. Bowel symptoms described as mild, with occasional cramps after eating. This is a temporal association, not an established medication adverse reaction.

timeline.title: Incomplete symptom relief reported
timeline.summary: User reported that ondansetron helped only a little and dose reductions helped only a little, and asked about reducing food aversion/anticipatory nausea. The drug reduced, dose, timing, hydration/nutrition status and subsequent management are not specified.

timeline.title: Latest available CBC and metabolic panel
timeline.summary: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL (low), albumin 3.3 g/dL (low), creatinine 0.4 mg/dL. WBC 9.3, absolute neutrophils 7.3 and platelets 345 ×10⁹/L.
timeline.details: October 20 CBC documents anemia (hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL) with WBC, absolute neutrophils, and platelets within the reporting laboratory ranges. October 20 CMP documents low albumin (3.3 g/dL), high total protein (8.9 g/dL), low chloride (96 mmol/L), mildly high anion gap (13 mmol/L); creatinine 0.4 mg/dL and liver enzymes within supplied ranges.

timeline.dateLabel: Clinical date not visible · available by 2026-09-24
timeline.title: S2 metastasis abutting the right S2 nerve root
timeline.summary: Enhancing right S2 sacral lesion approximately 1.5 x 1.4 x 1.5 cm, expanding sacrum and contacting/abutting right S2 nerve root.
timeline.details:
Adjacent non-masslike presacral enhancement could be metastatic or inflammatory.
Right piriformis enhancement/edema could reflect denervation edema.
Multiple additional sclerotic lumbar/pelvic lesions consistent with metastases as seen on prior CT.
Visualized spinal cord and cauda equina described as normal. Conus ends at approximately L1.
No substantial degenerative abnormalities described from T12-L1 through L5-S1; incidental left perineural cyst.
Normal visualized cauda equina does not erase the separate sacral root involvement.

timeline.dateLabel: Clinical date not visible · available by 2026-09-23
timeline.title: Sacral metastases with involvement of nerve exit openings
timeline.summary: Osseous metastatic lesion centered at right sacrum S2, with enhancing soft tissue involving multiple right greater than left neural foramina.
timeline.details:
Most pronounced at right S2 with partial effacement/mass effect on associated nerve root; possible projection into ventral thecal sac.
Signal abnormality involves bilateral S2 and possibly S3 foramina, with milder right S1 extension.
Smaller right S4 sacral metastatic lesion, approximately 1.2 x 0.7 cm in axial plane, with signal extending into the right S4 foramen.
Additional small pelvic/sacral lesions correlate with sclerotic foci on prior CT and are suspicious for additional osseous metastases.
Right-predominant presacral edema/enhancement near sacral nerve roots and mild right piriformis edema/enhancement, suspected neurogenic.
No definitive new osseous metastatic lesions stated in report body.
No hip joint effusion/high-grade cartilage defect or tendon tear; sacroiliac joints intact.
Extent into the thecal sac is possible, not definite. These findings should not be described merely as nonspecific hip pain.

timeline.dateLabel: Message date not visible · available by Sep 12, 2026
timeline.title: BNT326 + BNT327 waitlist and bridge plan
timeline.summary: Historical oncology correspondence described limited/unpredictable trial slots, a requested waitlist place and at least eight weeks after radiation before potential eligibility.
timeline.details: Restart chemotherapy after break, give two cycles, then repeat scans to assess response while exploring trial availability. The record does not confirm enrollment, present recruitment or receipt of this proposed plan.

timeline.dateLabel: 2026-09-04 · report signed date; acquisition date unavailable
timeline.title: Progression across lung, breast, and nodal sites
timeline.summary: Increasing left lower lobe and left hilar masslike consolidation, likely worsening tumor burden.
timeline.details:
Numerous new and enlarging pulmonary nodules in both lungs; nodular septal thickening suggestive of worsening lymphangitic carcinomatosis.
Left upper lobe nodule 0.7 x 0.6 cm, previously 0.6 x 0.5 cm; new right upper lobe nodule 0.4 cm.
Increased bilateral breast nodular enhancing soft tissue, skin thickening, discrete breast masses, and bilateral axillary/left subpectoral lymphadenopathy. Example medial right breast mass 1.4 x 1.0 cm, previously 0.7 x 0.8 cm.
Unchanged loculated left pleural effusion and pleural thickening, considered likely malignant on the report.
Pericardial thickening and enhancement with unchanged small effusion, concerning for pericardial metastatic disease.
Unchanged scattered sclerotic osseous lesions.
No lower cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Mediastinal soft tissue stranding without discrete measurable lymphadenopathy.
Lymphangitic carcinomatosis and pericardial metastatic disease are radiology impressions/suspicions, not tissue-confirmed diagnoses in this source.

timeline.dateLabel: Clinical date not visible · available by 2026-09-04
timeline.title: Enlarging left adrenal and upper abdominal nodal disease
timeline.summary: Enlarging left adrenal lesion interpreted as worsening adrenal metastasis.
timeline.details:
Enlarging upper abdominal lymph nodes suspicious for nodal metastases, including gastrohepatic and porta hepatis nodes; porta hepatis node 1.0 cm, previously 0.6 cm.
Unchanged sclerotic osseous lesions, without new aggressive osseous lesion.
No suspicious liver or renal masses; no hydronephrosis; no abnormal bowel dilation/wall thickening or free intraperitoneal air.
Gastrohepatic node's current size is clipped in the screenshot and has not been guessed.

timeline.title: Transient creatinine elevation reported
timeline.summary: Serum creatinine was 1.2 mg/dL and eGFR 59 on August 11, 2026. Family history reports normalization by August 18 (~0.6), but that specific dated chemistry result is not in the extracted series. Later verified values: 0.8 on Sep 8, 0.6 on Sep 14 and 0.4 on Oct 20.

timeline.title: Breast/axillary radiation planned
timeline.summary: A ten-fraction course was planned to the breast and axilla. Swelling and pain were reported after three sessions. The exact start date, total delivered fractions and completion date require the radiation treatment summary.

timeline.title: Lorlatinib hold for radiation
timeline.summary: A two-week lorlatinib hold during radiation was reported. Exact interval and restart date were not retained.

timeline.title: Brain MRI reported normal
timeline.summary: Family reported a normal August brain MRI. Do not infer brain status after the date of that scan. Original report not retrieved by this agent.

timeline.title: Symptoms during breast radiation
timeline.summary: Breast swelling, sternal tenderness, collarbone burning and left arm numbness were reported. These are symptoms, without a confirmed cause in the retained summary.

timeline.title: Pemetrexed alone during bevacizumab hold
timeline.summary: Pemetrexed alone was reported on July 21, with bevacizumab held. A maintenance plan of pemetrexed plus bevacizumab was discussed. Reason and exact duration of the bevacizumab hold are not confirmed.

timeline.dateLabel: 2026-07-10 · interpretation date; outside ultrasound performed July 2
timeline.title: Suspicious painful right breast mass
timeline.summary: Irregular hypoechoic mass at right breast 11 o'clock, 8 cm from nipple, measured at least 2.7 x 2.6 x 2.5 cm on submitted static images.
timeline.details:
Corresponds to hypermetabolic mass on PET/CT dated June 4, 2026.
Cine images suggested abnormality may be larger than static measurements; possible additional 1.5 cm and 1.1 cm superficial masses.
BI-RADS 4, suspicious; ultrasound-guided biopsy recommended if clinically indicated, with diagnostic mammography and second-look ultrasound to define extent.

timeline.dateLabel: July 2026 history; addendum clinical date not visible; available by July 24
timeline.title: Breast/axillary biopsy
timeline.summary: Right breast core biopsy: poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with mucinous features. CK7 positive, CK20 weak positive; Napsin A, TTF-1, GATA3, ER and PAX8 negative. The addendum favors pulmonary origin and considers a breast primary unlikely, but does not definitively establish origin; other origins cannot be entirely excluded. ALK is established by the separate FoundationOne report, not by this addendum.

timeline.title: Bevacizumab dose reported
timeline.summary: Bevacizumab administration on June 30 was listed as the last dose before a subsequent hold. It was later reported continuing by October 30.

timeline.title: Trial discussions
timeline.summary: Family reported that Dr. Jeffrey Clarke at Duke and Dr. Alice Shaw at Mass General favored BNT326 + BNT327 as a trial option. This is a historical discussion, not evidence of enrollment, current eligibility or current trial ranking.

timeline.title: Breast/axillary progression described
timeline.summary: Right breast lesion and axillary lymph nodes were described in May–June, with a small right lung lesion later. Original timing should be reconciled against the March 27 positive axillary biopsy. Do not label May–June the first metastatic progression. Some worsening was reported during treatment holds; causation is not established.

timeline.title: Chemotherapy began
timeline.summary: Retained history gives cycle 1 of carboplatin, pemetrexed and bevacizumab on April 21, 2026, every 21 days. The October 30 update reports two carboplatin rounds in total. Exact administration records were not retrieved.

timeline.title: Right axillary metastasis documented
timeline.summary: Right axillary lymph node biopsy showed metastatic adenocarcinoma with mucinous/clear-cell features. The associated PD-L1 report dated April 2, 2026 was <1%. This provides an earlier documented metastatic site than the May–June progression shorthand.

timeline.title: Follow-up after SBRT
timeline.summary: January CT was summarized as left lower lobe lesion unchanged with complete response elsewhere. Original scan wording and exact date need confirmation; avoid presenting this as a current complete remission.

timeline.title: Lorlatinib 75 mg maintenance
timeline.summary: 75 mg daily was reported during early 2026, later reduced to 50 mg during chemotherapy. Exact date of increase to 75 mg and subsequent reduction is not retained.

timeline.title: Chest wall pain after SBRT
timeline.summary: Post-SBRT chest wall pain, oxygen readings approximately 92–98%, and a mild pericardial effusion were reported. Timing and clinical interpretation require source confirmation.

timeline.title: Hip/buttock pain
timeline.summary: Severe pain with rising or coughing was reported, with walking/running painless and some seated/straight-leg maneuvers provoking pain. Oxycodone and acetaminophen reportedly helped. No diagnosis is established by these descriptions.

timeline.title: Radiation to left lower lobe
timeline.summary: SBRT to the left lower lobe over three fractions, reported December 29–31, 2025.

timeline.title: Pleural fluid improved
timeline.summary: CT chest reportedly showed trace left pleural effusion, no mediastinal/hilar adenopathy, stable nodules and sclerotic bone lesions, and unchanged small pericardial effusion. An 18 mm subpleural left lower lobe nodule was described as new or better seen after re-expansion.

timeline.title: PleurX removed
timeline.summary: Catheter removed following reported autopleurodesis. Exact removal date is not retained.

timeline.title: Pleural sampling negative for malignancy
timeline.summary: Pleural fluid cytology and pleural biopsy were reported negative for malignancy; biopsy showed reactive changes with rare atypical cells favored reactive, BAP1 retained and Claudin-4 negative. This later negative sampling does not erase the earlier positive pleural cytology.

timeline.title: PleurX placed
timeline.summary: Indwelling pleural catheter placed for recurrent left pleural effusion. Exact placement date is not retained.

timeline.title: Lorlatinib reduced
timeline.summary: Dose reduced to 50 mg daily in retained history.

timeline.title: Lorlatinib restarted
timeline.summary: Restarted at 100 mg with a steroid, according to retained history. Steroid identity, dose and indication are not confirmed.

timeline.title: Malignant pleural fluid
timeline.summary: Pleural cytology was reported to contain malignant cells; TTF-1 positive and weak BerEP4. Original report should establish exact sampling/result dates.

timeline.title: Early partial response
timeline.summary: CT was reported to show a partial response to lorlatinib.

timeline.title: Lorlatinib temporarily held
timeline.summary: Reported hold July 29 through August 3, followed by restart August 4. Reason for this particular hold is not reliably retained in the available summary.

timeline.title: Repeated pleural drainage
timeline.summary: Three thoracenteses were reported during July–August 2025, including drainage amounts of 1.5 L and 500 mL. Exact dates and all volumes are not available in the retained summary.

timeline.title: Lorlatinib started
timeline.summary: Started first-line lorlatinib 100 mg daily.

timeline.title: Baseline PET/CT
timeline.summary: Bulky mediastinal/left hilar disease with extensive neck, chest and upper abdominal lymph nodes, pleural lesions and small pleural effusion. No brain metastases reported at baseline.

timeline.title: Initial chest imaging
timeline.summary: CTA described a left perihilar/mediastinal mass and small left pleural effusion.

timeline.title: Stage IV ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma
timeline.summary: Reported initial diagnosis: stage IV ALK-positive non-small-cell lung adenocarcinoma, in a never-smoker. Exact diagnostic biopsy date requires the original report.

sources.note: Clinical/report date is not visible; screenshots were uploaded September 4, 2026. Report refers to a separately dictated same-day chest CT. Available in supplied files by 2026-09-04. Original retained privately.
sources.excerpt: Enlarging left adrenal lesion interpreted as worsening adrenal metastasis. Enlarging upper abdominal lymph nodes suspicious for nodal metastases, including gastrohepatic and porta hepatis nodes; porta hepatis node 1.0 cm, previously 0.6 cm. Unchanged sclerotic osseous lesions, without new aggressive osseous lesion. No suspicious liver or renal masses; no hydronephrosis; no abnormal bowel dilation/wall thickening or free intraperitoneal air.

sources.title: Pelvis MRI report screenshots
sources.note: MRI acquisition and report date are not visible. Upload date is not the clinical date. Available in supplied files by 2026-09-23. Original retained privately.
sources.excerpt: Osseous metastatic lesion centered at right sacrum S2, with enhancing soft tissue involving multiple right greater than left neural foramina. Most pronounced at right S2 with partial effacement/mass effect on associated nerve root; possible projection into ventral thecal sac. Signal abnormality involves bilateral S2 and possibly S3 foramina, with milder right S1 extension. Smaller right S4 sacral metastatic lesion, approximately 1.2 x 0.7 cm in axial plane, with signal extending into the right S4 foramen. Additional small pelvic/sacral lesions correlate with sclerotic foci on prior CT and are suspicious for additional osseous metastases. Right-predominant presacral edema/enhancement near sacral nerve roots and mild right piriformis edema/enhancement, suspected neurogenic. No definitive new osseous metastatic lesions stated in report body. No hip joint effusion/high-grade cartilage defect or tendon tear; sacroiliac joints intact.

sources.title: Lumbar spine MRI report screenshots
sources.note: MRI acquisition and report date are not visible. Report refers to a separately dictated pelvis MRI. Available in supplied files by 2026-09-24. Original retained privately.
sources.excerpt: Enhancing right S2 sacral lesion approximately 1.5 x 1.4 x 1.5 cm, expanding sacrum and contacting/abutting right S2 nerve root. Adjacent non-masslike presacral enhancement could be metastatic or inflammatory. Right piriformis enhancement/edema could reflect denervation edema. Multiple additional sclerotic lumbar/pelvic lesions consistent with metastases as seen on prior CT. Visualized spinal cord and cauda equina described as normal. Conus ends at approximately L1. No substantial degenerative abnormalities described from T12-L1 through L5-S1; incidental left perineural cyst.

sources.title: Outside right breast ultrasound second-opinion interpretation
sources.excerpt: Irregular hypoechoic mass at right breast 11 o'clock, 8 cm from nipple, measured at least 2.7 x 2.6 x 2.5 cm on submitted static images. Corresponds to hypermetabolic mass on PET/CT dated June 4, 2026. Cine images suggested abnormality may be larger than static measurements; possible additional 1.5 cm and 1.1 cm superficial masses. BI-RADS 4, suspicious; ultrasound-guided biopsy recommended if clinically indicated, with diagnostic mammography and second-look ultrasound to define extent.

sources.title: Right breast biopsy addendum screenshot
sources.note: Available in supplied files by 2026-07-24. Original retained privately.
sources.excerpt: Right breast core biopsy: poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with mucinous features. CK7 positive, CK20 weak positive; Napsin A, TTF-1, GATA3, ER and PAX8 negative. The addendum favors pulmonary origin and considers a breast primary unlikely, but does not definitively establish origin; other origins cannot be entirely excluded. ALK is established by the separate FoundationOne report, not by this addendum.

faq.q: What kind of cancer does Mayya have?
faq.a: The record describes stage IV ALK-positive non-small-cell lung adenocarcinoma. July 2026 breast tissue genomic testing confirmed an EML4–ALK fusion, variant 3a/b. The breast pathology addendum favors pulmonary origin and calls a breast primary unlikely, but the addendum alone is not definitive. The family has described the breast disease as lung cancer metastasis.

faq.q: What treatment is she taking now?
faq.a: The October 30 family update lists lorlatinib 50 mg, pemetrexed every three weeks and continuing bevacizumab (Avastin). Two previous carboplatin rounds were reported. The exact most recent infusion dates and most medication doses are not available.

HLA-A: A*26:01 and A*31:01. HLA-B: B*35:01 and B*35:02. HLA-C: C*04:01 and C*04:01. These class I results are from blood collected July 21, 2026 and reported July 29, page 3. HLA class II is not included.

faq.q: When was spread to the axilla documented?
faq.a: A right axillary lymph node collected March 27, 2026 is described as metastatic adenocarcinoma in the April 2 PD-L1 report. Earlier summaries focused on May–June, but that is not the earliest documented axillary disease.

faq.q: What do the mutation tests say?
faq.a: Keep each specimen separate. July blood testing reported EML4–ALK at 0.2%, tumor fraction 0.3%, TMB 3.8 mut/Mb and MSI-high not detected. July breast tissue confirmed variant 3a/b, but low tumor purity left tissue TMB, MSI and HRD indeterminate. Variants of uncertain significance and possible blood-cell-derived variants are listed separately.

faq.q: Why are some findings labeled unverified?
faq.a: Earlier conversations mention STK11, CDKN2A, MTAP and MET staining findings, but the original reports establishing those details were not retrieved for this compilation. They remain visible as reported history, with source confirmation pending.

No brain metastases were reported at baseline, and an August 2026 brain MRI was described by the family as normal. The original August report and a later brain MRI are not available here. This does not establish brain status after that scan.

faq.q: What is causing the food aversion?
faq.a: The cause has not been established. On October 30, nausea was reported from food thoughts, smells or offers, sometimes despite hunger. Onset followed starting duloxetine or changing to sublingual buprenorphine; the family was unsure which came first. A timing link alone does not prove a medication cause.

faq.q: Is she in a clinical trial?
faq.a: No enrollment is established in the available record. BNT326 + BNT327 was a family-reported preferred option discussed with Duke and Mass General in May 2026. Other trials and drugs were researched. Historical discussions and trial lists do not show current enrollment, recruitment or eligibility.

faq.q: Is this her complete medical chart?
faq.a: It compiles the available cancer history, treatment and medication history, symptoms, molecular results, imaging excerpts and lab trends. Full hospital records, allergies, all medication doses, radiation completion summaries and parts of her earlier medical history are missing. The evidence labels and open questions show those gaps.

faq.q: What do the latest available scans show?
faq.a: The chest CT report signed September 4 describes increasing left lower lobe/hilar disease, new or growing nodules in both lungs and worsening bilateral breast and nodal disease. It raises concern for lymphangitic and pericardial spread; those are radiology impressions, not tissue confirmation here. The abdomen CT screenshots describe an enlarging left adrenal metastasis and upper abdominal nodes. Sacral MRI screenshots available by September 23–24 describe S2 and S4 lesions and sacral nerve-root involvement. The MRI clinical dates are not visible. No later response scan is available in this compilation.

faq.q: What do the latest blood tests show?
faq.a: October 20: hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL and albumin 3.3 g/dL were low; WBC 9.3, absolute neutrophils 7.3 and platelets 345 ×10⁹/L were within the supplied reporting ranges. Creatinine was 0.4 mg/dL, eGFR 128. The full available latest components and selected trends are in Labs. These numbers do not by themselves establish treatment response.

uncertainties.title: Complete medical record not available

uncertainties.detail: Breast/axillary radiation was planned for ten fractions and had started. The final delivered fractions, dose and completion date are not verified. No sacral radiation completion record is available.

uncertainties.detail: August MRI was family-reported normal. No later brain imaging result is established.

uncertainties.title: Reported molecular findings need originals
uncertainties.detail: Exact reports for STK11, CDKN2A, MTAP and MET IHC findings were not retrieved. Do not treat these as confirmed by the July Guardant or August FoundationOne reports.

uncertainties.title: Disease response after reviewed scans
uncertainties.detail: Ongoing treatment in October does not establish response after the September CT and subsequent MRI screenshots.

uncertainties.title: Dates cropped out of some scans
uncertainties.detail: For the abdomen CT and sacral MRI screenshots, the record labels file-availability dates. They are not asserted as examination dates.

glossary.meaning: A gene change that can help drive this lung cancer. It is different from the HLA immune type.
Non-small-cell lung cancer, a broad lung cancer group. Adenocarcinoma is one type.
Cancer that has spread from its original site to another part of the body.
Fluid in the space around a lung.
Focused radiation delivered in a small number of treatment sessions.
Inherited immune-system markers. Some treatments or trials depend on a specific HLA type.
A genetic variant whose meaning is uncertain. Its presence alone does not establish a treatment target.
Tumor mutational burden, a test-specific measure of mutation count. Blood and tissue results should stay separate.
A laboratory stain that looks for proteins in tissue. It is different from DNA sequencing.
Cancer spread involving lymph channels in the lung. The September CT wording says suspected.
